ECE 6390 / Spacecraft systems

Electric thrust

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows the trade between high exhaust speed, propellant savings and thrust at a fixed power.

A steady directed exhaust carries momentum at rate F = ṁvₑ. Its kinetic power is ½ṁvₑ², supplied here by a fraction η of electrical input power P.

Combining the relations gives F = 2ηP/vₑ and ṁ = 2ηP/vₑ². At fixed electrical power, higher exhaust speed reduces both thrust and propellant flow.

The approximation Δv ≈ Ft/m estimates acceleration time when spacecraft mass changes little. A long continuous orbital maneuver also depends on thrust direction and changing orbit geometry.

Example

For P = 1,000 W, η = 0.60, and vₑ = 30,000 m/s, thrust is 0.040 N and mass flow is approximately 1.33 × 10⁻⁶ kg/s.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. At fixed power and efficiency, how do thrust and mass flow change if exhaust speed doubles?

    Track the first and second powers of vₑ in the two formulas.

    Thrust halves, while mass flow becomes one quarter. The trade saves propellant flow at the cost of acceleration and usually a longer maneuver.
